cq_coverage.details: All competency questions are fully addressed. The ontology provides explicit classes and properties for invoices, organizations, roles, addresses, items, prices, identifiers, document structure, and business process assignment. The use of both direct and reified relations supports comprehensive querying for all CQs.

strengths: Deep, multi-level hierarchy from EDIFACTInterchange to Data Elements
Comprehensive use of restrictions (including minCardinality for mandatory sections)
General class axioms and equivalence for core concepts (e.g., Invoice)
Rich disjointness and disjoint union axioms
Technical segment types (BGM, NAD) can be subclassed as needed
weaknesses: No explicit rdfs:seeAlso/skos:example CQ traceability annotations (documentation enhancement only)
No owl:hasKey or additional identity axioms for Invoice uniqueness (minor, as not strictly required for CQ coverage)

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Add rdfs:seeAlso or skos:example annotations referencing which classes/properties answer each CQ.
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Enhances documentation and traceability for ontology users and maintainers.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Consider using owl:hasKey or additional equivalence axioms to define Invoice uniqueness (e.g., by reference number and date).
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Supports instance identity reasoning and de-duplication in knowledge graphs.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: If segment-specific constraints are needed, formally subclass BGM and NAD as EDIFACTSegment subclasses.
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Facilitates segment-type specific queries and constraints, but not critical unless technical validation is required.

suggestions_addressed: Add explicit minCardinality restrictions for mandatory properties (e.g., Invoice must have at least one InvoiceHeader, InvoiceDetail, and InvoiceSummary section).
Model BGM and NAD as subclasses of EDIFACTSegment to allow segment-specific constraints and facilitate querying for segment types.
suggestions_ignored: Add rdfs:seeAlso or skos:example annotations referencing which classes/properties answer each CQ.
Increase use of owl:hasKey or additional equivalence axioms for identifying unique instances (e.g., Invoice uniquely identified by reference number and date).
improvement_tracking.notes: High-priority modeling improvements (mandatory section cardinality and segment subclassing) were implemented, raising quality to near-perfect. Documentation and identity suggestions remain open but are not critical for core CQ or constraint fulfillment.

summary: The ontology is now highly mature, fully covering all competency questions with deep, well-structured hierarchies, correct use of restrictions, disjointness, and technical fidelity to EDIFACT. All critical modeling and constraint adherence issues are resolved. Remaining suggestions are minor documentation and instance identity improvements, which do not affect CQ or validator compliance.
